purpose: Primary-source repository research for a reusable GitHub template; original observations, not endorsement or a full audit.

discovery.scope: Every unique public repository returned by all paginated supported search results. The connector does not expose total_count or incomplete_results; newly unindexed, hidden, deleted or changed repositories cannot be ruled out.
discovery.failed_route: Raw search/readme REST routes were rejected; supported repository search and per-repository contents/file reads were used.

methodology: Fetched repository metadata separately to verify description, fork parent and archive flags.
Read primary README openings for every nonempty discoverable README, including alternate case/names; where absent/blank, inspected a selected primary file or manifest and recorded empty cases.

Selected seven relevant repositories for source/config/test inspection. File URLs are pinned to branch head commits fetched during research; ordinary overview URLs retain branch links with captured file blob SHA.
Fetched remote text only. Did not clone, install, build, run tests, invoke hooks, execute code, submit issues or alter account/repository settings.
Fork contents are attributed to their upstream authors; ownership in this account does not establish original authorship. Historical docs are not current dependency/version recommendations.

deep_inspections.adapt: Keep a concise command/contract map, validate generated artifacts with the consuming tool, and make required-check aggregation include every required job.
findings: Compiler phases are mapped to concrete files; option validation throws descriptive errors before processing.
Generated declarations are snapshot-tested and independently compiled by TypeScript under strict options. Invalid-input cases assert rejection rather than recording error text as success.
CI separately exercises built package compatibility, a minimum runtime, fuzz seeds and corpus/spec output. The Claude workflow is triggered by explicit @claude text and needs a secret.
Static integration defect: ci-ok depends on build, bun, engines, fuzz and output but checks only build/fuzz/output results. Its comment overstates the aggregate guarantee.
deep_inspections.name: json-schema-to-typescript
deep_inspections.reject: Do not copy the secret-dependent mention workflow, auto-publish policy, package stack, action tags or incomplete aggregate check as universal defaults.

deep_inspections.adapt: Verify visible behavior and cleanup across lifecycle transitions, and distinguish declared test coverage from commands actually executed.
findings: Public Store interface carries key/value relationships; StoreSnapshot and StoreDefinition separate observed state from updates.
Connected store owns its subscription and unsubscribes during unmount; browser tests check rendered values after clicks and missing-provider failure.
Memory benchmark records allocate/unmount/snapshot steps and explicitly leaves CI automation unfinished.
Static CI mismatch: matrix declares operating systems but runs-on is fixed to ubuntu-latest. Bad-case Flow files exist, but the inspected npm test path does not call their shell runner.
deep_inspections.name: undux
deep_inspections.reject: Do not install React/RxJS for a neutral template or describe a declared OS matrix/manual memory profile as verified coverage.

deep_inspections.adapt: For hooks, test both matching/nonmatching events, repeat invocation and cleanup; enable relevant diagnostics explicitly with clear cost/behavior.
findings: Emitter<K> connects channel names to message value types; optional development mode supplies runtime cycle diagnostics.
Tests include event delivery, emission before subscription, listener disposal, sequential subscribe/unsubscribe and cycle/noncycle cases.
Cycle detection is disabled by default and is a local diagnostic, not security enforcement. Tests mix observable behavior with some internal-map assertions.
deep_inspections.name: typed-rx-emitter
deep_inspections.reject: Do not infer that every available diagnostic or agent is always executed; avoid importing the old Node/CircleCI/TSLint stack.

deep_inspections.adapt: Test default handling using absent, null, empty and false values so hook/config flags do not collapse distinct meanings.
findings: Option/Some/None make missing data and fallback paths explicit in public types.
Tests specifically distinguish null/undefined from 0, false and empty string, and cover a NaN fallback policy.
Behavioral algebra laws are tested alongside concrete examples; these are deterministic examples rather than an exhaustive proof.
deep_inspections.name: tsoption
deep_inspections.reject: No requirement to introduce an Option dependency or functional-programming vocabulary into every project.

deep_inspections.adapt: Keep initialization reviewable, propagate command failures, test failure paths and verify generated content, including no-op and overwrite behavior.
findings: Generator substitutes project identity from existing npm/git configuration into a template and then attempts dependency installation.

The command helper catches failures and returns an empty string; therefore the outer yarn-to-npm catch cannot observe a failed yarn install. This is a static inference from the code, not an executed reproduction.
The root README, src/cli.ts and test/test.ts are blank. Template compiler strictness and named test scripts do not establish a tested initializer.
deep_inspections.name: create-typescript-app
deep_inspections.reject: Do not copy silent failures, automatic package installation, global-configuration requirements or blank tests as production defaults.

deep_inspections.adapt: Use a minimal host smoke probe to distinguish discovery from invocation, and validate real request/response behavior against current host documentation.
findings: Small stdio server explicitly registers its tool and resource capabilities and rejects unknown tool/resource names.
The declared ping input is required, but the handler does not inspect it; the result uses content: [] with an extra toolResult field.
Manifest provides a build command and strict compiler configuration; the root tree contains no tests.
deep_inspections.name: mcp-ping
deep_inspections.reject: Do not treat this historical sample as a current MCP conformance reference or preinstall the server for every template consumer.

deep_inspections.adapt: Separate fast local feedback, schema checks, behavioral checks and host/OS permissions. Test that rejected hook/config operations leave state unchanged.
findings: This is a fork of anthropics/sandbox-runtime, with upstream authorship/license retained.
Pre-commit runs lint-staged for TypeScript formatting/linting. Runtime configuration is separately parsed with Zod and reports field-specific failures.
Filesystem read/write and network defaults have different semantics, explicitly documented in internal interfaces. Selected Linux code adds mandatory deny paths with worktree/symlink handling.

Selected tests assert both failing exit status and unchanged protected file contents; configuration tests reject invalid domains, paths and incompatible options. Cross-platform CI is visible; none was executed here.
deep_inspections.name: sandbox-runtime
deep_inspections.reject: Do not label a Git/agent hook a sandbox. Do not carry over filesystem-disabled, weaker-isolation, privileged runner or system-setting changes as template defaults.
